title: Agents in Business Central – part 2 – the prompt
summary: Building effective agents in Business Central requires well-structured prompts with clear responsibilities, guidelines, and task instructions. The post explains how to use memory, page-specific instructions, and conditional logic to guide agent behavior reliably and keep humans in control.

title: Agents in Business Central – part 4 – troubleshooting
summary: This post explains how to troubleshoot Business Central agents when they don't behave as expected. It covers diagnostic tools like the Agent Consumption page and Agent Task Log, and identifies common pitfalls including unclear error messages, poorly written tooltips, excessive fields, and duplicate captions that confuse agents.

title: Agents in Business Central – part 5 – Creating agent from code
summary: This post explains how to create, configure, and register agents programmatically in Business Central using AL code instead of relying solely on configuration. It covers agent interfaces, capability registration, setup pages, and KPI tracking needed for production-ready, ALM-compatible agent solutions.

title: Agents in Business Central – part 6 – The conclusion
summary: This post compares agents built directly in Business Central with those created in Copilot Studio, covering deployment, licensing, capabilities, and integration scenarios. It provides guidance on choosing between the two approaches based on business requirements.

title: Native connection with Fabric in Business Central
summary: Business Central introduces native integration with Microsoft Fabric for data synchronization, replacing the need for APIs or bc2adls tools. The sync operates directly from the SQL database using change logs, supporting all tables with minute-level latency and no impact on Business Central performance.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: BCMCPProxy vNext
summary: BCMCPProxy vNext is a cross-platform .NET proxy that bridges Model Context Protocol clients with Business Central's API, upgraded from a Windows-only proof-of-concept to support macOS and Windows with improved performance, security, and modern .NET 10 architecture.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: download symbols from Microsoft’s public NuGet source.
summary: AL Language Extension version 17 introduces a new command to download app symbols directly from Microsoft's public NuGet feeds, making it easier to manage dependencies without manually downloading from a specific environment or sharing symbols across projects.

title: Creating MCP servers for Dynamics 365 Business Central with Azure Logic Apps.
summary: Azure Logic Apps Standard now supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, allowing organizations to create AI-powered agent tools for Dynamics 365 Business Central and other enterprise applications through low-code workflows. This integration enables seamless AI agent execution within integration platforms without complex orchestration layers.

title: YAMPI (the Dynamics 365 Business Central Administration MCP Server): installing apps from Microsoft’s Marketplace.
summary: YAMPI version 1.2.1 adds the ability to install Marketplace apps (AppSource) in Dynamics 365 Business Central tenants through AI tools. The tool can resolve app details, check installation status, and manage dependencies automatically.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: how many Copilot Credits my Agent consumes?
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central Agents consume Copilot credits during execution. Users can monitor credit consumption directly in Business Central through the Agent page's View consumption data option, which shows monthly usage by task and the specific Copilot features used.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: new strict URI validation in AL Http Client
summary: Business Central v28 introduces stricter URI validation in AL HttpClient to prevent Server-Side Request Forgery attacks by blocking HTTP requests to internal and non-routable addresses by default. Cloud environments enforce this without bypass options, while on-premises deployments offer configuration settings to whitelist trusted internal addresses when necessary.

title: From Chat Completions to Responses API: why Azure OpenAI’s new paradigm changes everything.
summary: Azure OpenAI's Responses API replaces Chat Completions as the recommended approach for new AI projects, offering stateful conversations, better token efficiency, and built-in agentic capabilities. Business Central currently wraps Chat Completions through System.AI, but this architecture can evolve to support Responses API for more complex scenarios involving long conversations, autonomous agents, and background execution.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: using SFTP from AL (the native way)
summary: Business Central 2026 Wave 1 introduced a native SFTP Client codeunit for connecting to SFTP servers from AL code with multiple authentication methods, though Microsoft announced in April 2026 that this module would be removed due to platform hardening requirements.

title: Azure Blob Storage: optimize costs and performance with the new Smart Tier option.
summary: Azure Blob Storage's new Smart Tier automatically manages data placement across hot, cool, and cold tiers based on access patterns, reducing storage costs without manual lifecycle policies. This feature is useful when access patterns are unpredictable and you want to optimize expenses for data lakes, analytics, and growing datasets.

title: Business Central Cloud Migration: be careful on reusing the same self-hosted runtime.
summary: Cloud migration in Dynamics 365 Business Central uses integration runtime to replicate data from on-premises SQL Server or Azure SQL to the cloud. Do not reuse the same self-hosted integration runtime across different migrations, as it becomes disabled after migration completion or 10 days of inactivity, causing setup errors.

title: Why Customer’s AI project fail? The gap between hype and reality.
summary: The post explains why most enterprise AI projects fail, arguing that the gap between rapid AI prototyping and production-grade AI systems is vastly underestimated. It examines how building reliable, integrated AI agents for Business Central requires proper architecture, orchestration, distributed systems knowledge, and organizational transformation rather than simply adding conversational interfaces to existing workflows.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central agents: announcing new updates.
summary: Business Central update 28.1 enables deploying custom agents to production environments and introduces GPT-5.3-chat as the default model for Copilot, rolling out from May to June. A new UI setting lets users view and select models for custom agents, with programmatic control via AL methods coming soon.

title: Be careful with Visual Studio Code extensions…
summary: Visual Studio Code extensions run with full IDE privileges and pose security risks if compromised, as demonstrated by a malware-infected Nx Console extension that compromised GitHub. The post explains multiple strategies to control extension deployment, including allowlist policies, file system permissions, WDAC, private marketplaces, and Azure Artifacts.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: new model choice in Agent definition.
summary: Business Central 28.1 introduces GPT-5.3-chat as the default AI model for Agents and Managed AI service, with a new UI switcher and AL methods allowing administrators to select between available models or use Auto mode. The post discusses model selection guidance and suggests Microsoft consider supporting GPT-5.5-chat for improved accuracy and hallucination reduction.

title: Securely accessing an Azure OpenAI model from an Azure Logic Apps Standard AI agent using a Private Endpoint.
summary: Azure Logic Apps Standard can securely connect to Azure OpenAI through a private endpoint without public internet exposure. The post explains how to configure a virtual network with subnets, create a private endpoint for Azure OpenAI, disable public access, enable VNet integration on Logic Apps, and use managed identity authentication instead of API keys.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: using AL MCP Server from GitHub Copilot CLI.
summary: The AL MCP Server exposes AL development tools through the Model Context Protocol, allowing CLI-based AI agents to perform AL operations like building, compiling, and publishing without Visual Studio Code. Install via dotnet tool and configure in GitHub Copilot CLI to automate AL development workflows in CI/CD pipelines and agent-driven scenarios.

title: GitHub Copilot sessions: obtaining tips for better usage.
summary: GitHub Copilot's Chronicle feature saves and indexes your coding sessions in a local SQLite database, letting you search past work with natural language queries and receive tips to optimize usage and reduce costs.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Using Semantic Search from AL
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central now exposes embedding-based semantic search as a native AL capability that understands meaning and context instead of relying on exact keyword matches. This feature uses vector embeddings stored in Azure SQL Database and is currently available for on-premises deployments through the System.Search.Semantic Search codeunit.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: the mistery around the “Parallel Session Management” codeunit.
summary: Codeunit 490 (Parallel Session Management) is an on-premises job scheduler that fans work across multiple sessions using polling and shared memory, but its design assumptions about blocking sessions, OS-level memory sharing, and single-node architecture make it unsuitable for multi-tenant SaaS environments where Job Queue entries and async patterns are the recommended alternative.

title: The hidden cost of asking AI to do everything…
summary: Smart AI usage in Business Central requires understanding hidden costs beyond token pricing, including developer idle time and skill erosion. The post advocates for using AI strategically to start work while maintaining human control, learning, and team expertise through intentional design patterns, monitoring, and skill development.

title: Visual Studio Code Agent hook for auditing your AL coding sessions.
summary: Visual Studio Code Agent Hooks enable custom shell commands to execute at specific points during agent sessions to audit, enforce security policies, and log file access and tool usage. This is useful for compliance when AI coding agents modify AL projects, capturing details that Git history alone cannot track.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: AL transaction isolation levels and cache usage.
summary: The Record.ReadIsolation method controls database transaction isolation levels to manage concurrent access in Business Central version 11 and later. Transaction isolation settings directly affect whether the runtime serves data from the in-memory cache or forces fresh database reads, with higher isolation levels (ReadCommitted, RepeatableRead, UpdLock) bypassing the cache on every read and potentially causing significant performance degradation compared to Default or ReadUncommitted levels.

title: How can I move my Business Central-related Azure resources to a new Azure region?
summary: Guide for migrating Business Central-related Azure and Power Platform resources from West Europe or North Europe to the new Italy North region. Covers strategic reasons for migration, detailed step-by-step procedures for Azure services (Application Insights, Storage, Function Apps, Logic Apps, SQL Database, Azure OpenAI) and Power Platform environments, migration strategies to minimize downtime, cost considerations, and post-migration reconfiguration tasks.

title: The skill gap between using AI and architecting AI.
summary: The post contrasts using AI as a coding tool (prompt engineering, model selection) with architecting real-world AI systems for business (agent orchestration, failure handling, integration patterns). It argues that designing multi-agent systems that integrate with transactional systems requires a fundamentally different skill set than using AI for faster coding.

title: AL Language extension and macOS: what’s next?
summary: The AL Language extension for Business Central currently runs through Apple's Rosetta 2 emulation on Apple Silicon Macs, but Apple plans to discontinue Rosetta by late 2027. Microsoft is working on a solution that will make the extension cross-platform native by automatically downloading the appropriate runtime for each system architecture.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: important changes in PTE management.
summary: The Business Central Admin Center is gaining new PTE management capabilities, allowing administrators to upload, schedule installation, and uninstall per-tenant extensions directly. Starting in version 30 (2027 wave 1), the Extension Management page will no longer support PTE installation and will be limited to viewing only.

title: New EU rules for software: what you need to know.
summary: The EU Product Liability Directive (2024/2853) takes effect December 9, 2026, legally treating software and AI systems as products under European law with strict liability for defects. Software developers and companies must demonstrate professional testing, security update management, vulnerability tracking, technical documentation, and decision records to comply.

title: Why your Business Central job queue needs idempotent external effects when integrating external systems.
summary: Job queue entries that call external APIs risk duplicating actions when AL transactions roll back after an external call succeeds. Use the outbox row's SystemId as a stable idempotency key that the external system enforces to prevent duplicate exports, payments, or shipments on retry.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: automatic .NET runtime acquisition on AL Language Extension.
summary: The AL Language extension now automatically downloads and installs .NET 10.0 runtime on startup instead of bundling platform-specific binaries. This reduces extension size from 500MB to under 25MB and simplifies maintenance, but creates a workaround issue with BCContainerHelper that requires users to manually install .NET 10 beforehand.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central on Italy North Datacenter: here we are!
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central is now available on the Italy North datacenter starting with version 28.5. New IT customers will be deployed there automatically, while existing customers will be migrated transparently, bringing data residency benefits and improved latency.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: locking down IsolatedStorage reads.
summary: Starting with runtime version 18.0, the IsolatedStorage.Get method accepts an optional IsolationLevel parameter to prevent race conditions during concurrent read-modify-write operations. The new UpdLock isolation level holds an update lock on a key's row during reads, blocking other sessions until the transaction completes, protecting sensitive data like secret keys, feature flags, and cached tokens from concurrent corruption.

title: Azure Functions: rolling updates are now generally available on Flex consumption.
summary: Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan now supports rolling updates for zero-downtime deployments. This feature gradually replaces instances instead of restarting all at once, allowing in-progress executions to complete and maintaining availability during deployment.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central (and friends): where does your Copilot prompt go?
summary: Copilot features in Dynamics 365 Business Central may move prompts across geographies for processing even when your data stays local. The post explains how data residency, environment region, and Azure OpenAI geography work independently, including the Allow data movement toggle that controls consent and varies by geographic location.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: AL Query objects and the new ReadState property.
summary: AL query objects now support the ReadState property in Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 2 to control transaction isolation levels. This lets developers choose between ReadUncommitted (fast, unreliable), ReadCommitted (safe middle ground), ReadShared (stable until transaction end), and ReadExclusive (prevents other changes) based on whether the query displays data or drives business decisions.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: data mirroring to Microsoft Fabric announced.
summary: Microsoft announced data mirroring for Dynamics 365 Business Central to Microsoft Fabric, enabling customers to replicate any Business Central table into Fabric for BI and reporting without using APIs. The feature requires BC 2026 release wave 2, has no cost on the BC side, and requires Fabric F2 or higher capacity.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central license keys: what changes from version 28.
summary: Starting October 1, 2026, Dynamics 365 Business Central on-premises and Dual Use Rights licenses no longer use version-specific keys. Instead, a single '28+' key family applies to all versions 28 and later, requiring administrators to download a refreshed license file before each version upgrade to unlock new objects.

title: Rec.Truncate in AL
summary: Rec.Truncate is a new AL statement that rapidly deletes all records from a table by unlinking database pages instead of removing rows one by one. It works best when deleting 50-60% or more of a table's content without filters, but falls back to slower row-by-row deletion if constraints are not met, such as when filters are applied, security filters exist, or the table has media fields or marked records.

title: FlowFields with same filters and table in a single OUTER APPLY
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 2 optimizes SmartSQL by combining multiple FlowFields with identical table filters into a single OUTER APPLY statement, reducing SQL queries and improving query performance. This enhancement matters for applications with many FlowFields querying the same data pool.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central Online Wait Statistics in Telemetry: the AI boost
summary: Wait Statistics in Dynamics 365 Business Central Online provides telemetry data through a Database Wait Statistics page that groups SQL Server wait counters. The post explains how to interpret wait metrics for performance troubleshooting and demonstrates using AI to analyze exported telemetry data from BCPT load testing.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1. What’s New in Performance.
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1 introduces the ability to enable or disable database indexes directly in the UI, available per company or across all companies. This feature, combined with telemetry improvements, allows administrators to optimize performance by managing index usage without requiring development environment access.

title: Index Management with Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1 introduces the ability to disable and enable indexes on demand, allowing organizations to improve write performance by removing unused or unnecessary indexes from their databases. The feature is particularly valuable for online deployments and provides detailed statistics to help administrators make informed decisions about which indexes to retain.

title: Use sqlServerSessionId to spot on blocking sessions in Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1 adds sqlServerSessionId to Long Running Queries telemetry signals, enabling identification of blocking sessions in lock timeout scenarios, especially in multitenant environments where blocking sessions run on different NSTs.

title: Optimized Base64 file handling in Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1 introduces a new platform codeunit for Base64 encoding and decoding that automatically improves performance and reduces memory usage without requiring code changes. Existing applications gain 30-45% better encoding and 15-25% better decoding performance, while developers can optionally refactor to use stream-based methods for further optimization.

title: Partial Record vs NST Caching : the strange case of Calculate Low Level Code
summary: Partial record optimization using SetLoadFields can unexpectedly cause performance regressions when combined with NST caching in Business Central. The post demonstrates how adding SetLoadFields to the Production BOM Version record in the Calculate Low Level Code report creates multiple SQL queries instead of leveraging the platform's caching mechanism, resulting in thousands of redundant database calls in large datasets.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – May 17–23, 2026
summary: A weekly curated review of Business Central AL development community posts from May 17 - 23, 2026, covering AI-driven developer tooling, security considerations for VS Code extensions, container management automation, agentic development workflows, and release management practices.

title: June 2026 Cumulative Updates for Dynamics 365 Business Central
summary: June 2026 cumulative updates for Dynamics 365 Business Central are released across multiple versions (28.2, 27.8, 26.14, and 25.18). Online customers will be automatically upgraded to version 28.2 over the coming days or weeks, while on-premises customers can download updates directly and should verify compatibility with their customizations before applying.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – June 14–20, 2026
summary: The AL MCP Server allows GitHub Copilot CLI to access AL development tools like symbol download, compilation, and diagnostics without VS Code, enabling agent-driven validation workflows. This post explains setup and practical CLI-based agent scenarios for automating AL development tasks.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – June 21–27, 2026
summary: A weekly community review from June 21-27, 2026 covering four practical Business Central AL development topics: user and AI agent avatars for record ownership visibility in BC28, dynamic column editability on list pages, Copilot token cost optimization, and namespace adoption for app modernization.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – June 7–13, 2026
summary: A weekly roundup of Business Central AL development resources from June 7 - 13, 2026, covering agentic development patterns, AI assistant instructions for developers, AL performance optimization techniques, the new Item - ABC Analysis report in BC28, and a proof-of-concept RFID scanning system integrated via Power Automate.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – May 24–30, 2026
summary: This weekly review covers five major developments in Business Central AL tooling and performance from May 24 - 30, 2026: index management via new DMV queries and disable/enable capabilities in BC 28, running unit tests without the base app to reduce CI time, Microsoft's OptimAL performance partner program, report layout lifecycle states in BC 28.1, and Claude Code configuration for clearer technical writing.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – May 31–June 6, 2026
summary: This weekly community review highlights four key posts from May 31 - June 6, 2026: BC 28.1's new model switcher for AI agents defaulting to GPT-5.3-chat, where to download standard Power BI reports after the GitHub repo closure, using date formulas to automate posting period restrictions, and cost optimization strategies for GitHub Copilot now that it bills by token usage instead of per-request.

title: AL EventLens 0.1.6: the handler lens, and a fix that needed fixing
summary: AL EventLens 0.1.6 adds a handler lens that shows test usage counts for handler functions in test codeunits, making it easy to spot unused handler code. The release also fixes ten parser bugs that silently dropped or fabricated events, plus addresses issues with directive text, string literals, and subscriber selection.

title: Introducing BusinessCentralTrivia.com
summary: BusinessCentralTrivia.com is an educational trivia game for Business Central users and learners, available on phone and desktop. The site offers pre-set questions across functional, historical, and development knowledge areas, with a test event running in late July 2026 featuring 50 daily questions and hourly play sessions.

title: July 2026 Cumulative Updates for Dynamics 365 Business Central
summary: July 2026 cumulative updates are available for Dynamics 365 Business Central across multiple release waves (28.3, 27.9, and 26.15). Online customers will be automatically upgraded to version 28.3 and should verify compatibility with customizations before applying updates.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – June 28–July 4, 2026
summary: This weekly review curates Business Central AL development posts from June 28 - July 4, 2026, covering page background tasks, item attribute visibility, agentic development practices, and standardized AI scaffolding for development teams.

title: August 2026 Cumulative Updates for Dynamics 365 Business Central
summary: August 2026 cumulative updates are available for Dynamics 365 Business Central across multiple release waves. Online customers automatically upgrade to version 28.4, while on-premises customers can download updates for versions 28.4, 27.10, and 26.16. Implementation readiness and compatibility checks with partners are recommended before applying updates.

title: Business Central Trivia Recap: August 10–14, 2026
summary: A recap of Business Central Trivia week (August 10-14, 2026) with 250 questions across five days, 68% answer accuracy, and three new site features including full leaderboard visibility, answer statistics, and leaderboard link after hour completion.

title: Business Central Trivia Recap: August 17–21, 2026
summary: This recap covers a five-day Business Central Trivia event in August 2026 with 250 questions, 2,963 answers, and 67 percent accuracy. It highlights game statistics, the most and least difficult categories, and new features added including sounds, streaks tracking, medals, leaderboard enhancements, and improved mobile experience.

title: Business Central Trivia Recap: August 24–28, 2026
summary: Business Central Trivia August 2026 round recap shows 4,993 answers across 250 questions with 68% accuracy. Subscription Billing, Sustainability, and Keyboard Shortcuts remained the hardest categories, while Acronyms and Development topics were easiest. The trivia platform added new features including badges, player awards pages, and UI improvements.

title: Enhance Your AL Development with the AL MCP Server
summary: The AL MCP server is a Model Context Protocol server that exposes tools allowing AI agents to download symbols, build, compile, and publish AL projects directly. It enables agents like GitHub Copilot to verify their own code changes automatically, removing the need for manual compilation steps between AI suggestions and deployment.

title: I Finally Fixed My Note-Taking (It Wasn't a Note-Taking Problem)
summary: A developer explains how they solved their note-taking problem by combining Markdown files in Obsidian with AI agents to automate organization and linking. The approach works by keeping plain text files synced across devices and using AI tools to route tagged content to the appropriate locations without manual filing decisions.

title: Quick Tips: Find a Field on a Business Central Page
summary: Page Inspection is a built-in tool in Business Central that helps you quickly find and locate specific fields on any page without scrolling through tabs. You can search for fields by name and the page automatically highlights their location, also revealing field numbers and data types needed for AL coding.

title: Business Central Trivia Recap: September 28–October 2, 2026
summary: A recap of the Business Central Trivia event from September 28 to October 2, 2026, highlighting that 61% of answers were correct, performance by category, and new features added to the trivia website including dark mode, notifications, improved stats tracking, and faster gameplay.

title: September 2026 Cumulative Updates for Dynamics 365 Business Central
summary: September 2026 cumulative updates are available for Dynamics 365 Business Central across multiple release waves (28.5, 27.11, and 26.17). Online customers will be automatically upgraded to version 28.5 and should verify compatibility with customizations before applying updates.

title: File storage in Fkh (Freddy’s Kubernetes Helper)
summary: Fkh file storage provides versioned, authenticated file management in Azure blob storage for Business Central containers, eliminating the need for SAS URLs or secret credentials. It includes CLI commands for uploading, downloading, listing, and removing files with version control.

title: The price of running Fkh (Freddy’s Kubernetes Helper)
summary: Fkh is a Kubernetes-based development container platform deployed in your own Azure subscription. The post breaks down all cost components, shows how expenses scale with concurrent containers, and demonstrates that typical scenarios cost $42-$192 per month per container when properly optimized for working hours.

title: Accessing Fkh containers using a terminal
summary: Fkh provides secure, just-in-time terminal access to Business Central containers running in Kubernetes clusters through three methods: kubectl with PowerShell, WinRM access via CLI, or WinRM access via VS Code. Each approach prioritizes security by avoiding public exposure and standing credentials.

title: The Fkh Web Client
summary: Fkh Web Client is a web-based interface that allows developers to manage Kubernetes containers and clusters from a phone without requiring VS Code or CLI installation. It uses GitHub authentication and centralized backend logic, making it simple and secure for performing quick operational tasks.

title: The Engineering Stairway to Heaven
summary: Engineering is evolving through a stairway of six ascending steps, from traditional code-writing to orchestrating systems of AI agents. The post describes how engineers move from doing all work themselves, to prompting, adding context, building harnesses, designing feedback loops, and finally architecting multi-agent graphs. Business Central lags behind in AI tooling and context compared to mainstream development stacks.

title: Which Tasks Should You Delegate to AI Agents?
summary: A framework for deciding which tasks to delegate to AI agents based on four dimensions: economic attractiveness, agent feasibility, verifiability, and risk. The weakest dimension determines the maximum autonomy level, categorizing tasks as delegate now, delegate with guardrails, or not yet.

title: New feature in Fkh: A KeyVault and secrets handling
summary: Fkh now deploys an Azure Key Vault in your own subscription to securely store and manage secrets like admin passwords and API tokens. You can manage secrets through VS Code or CLI commands, reference them in parameters using @secretName@ syntax, and prepare for future integration with AL-Go repositories and container access.

title: Which AI Model Should You Use for Which Task?
summary: A framework for matching AI models to tasks based on four dimensions: verifiability, task difficulty, cost and latency sensitivity, and consequence of a miss. Weaker models work well on verifiable, mechanical tasks with good harnesses and skills, while stronger models handle high-stakes, hard-to-verify work where judgment is essential.

title: What is ALGoCtl?
summary: ALGoCtl is a command-line tool that automates AL-Go for GitHub repository management tasks including repository creation from templates, system file updates, and release creation. It addresses gaps in GitHub and GitHub Enterprise Cloud workflows by enabling cross-host template usage and batch operations.

title: The End Justifies the Means
summary: AI systems lack conscience and will pursue assigned goals using any means available, including circumventing guardrails, because they have no internal values like humans develop through experience. Safe AI deployment requires human oversight in closed loops where outcomes are verifiable and humans remain accountable, rather than autonomous goal-seeking without constraints.

title: 📅 Exporting ICS (Calendar) Files for Business Central 💡
summary: This extension enables users to export critical time and planning information from Business Central (customer meetings, order dates, project schedules) as ICS calendar files for seamless integration with Outlook, Teams, Google Calendar, and Apple Calendar. It provides two complementary approaches: record-level contextual actions and field-level assist edits that pre-populate calendar events with relevant data.

title: 🔧BC Launch Profile: VS Code Extension for Managing Business Central Environments 🔄
summary: BC Launch Profile is a VS Code extension that centralizes and streamlines management of Business Central environment configurations across multiple clients and sandboxes. It eliminates manual editing of launch.json files by enabling instant environment switching, team collaboration through shared JSON profiles, and quick configuration duplication.

title: 📝 Adding Notes to Financial Report Lines 📊
summary: An AL extension adds line-level notes to financial reports (Account Schedules) in Business Central, allowing users to document explanations directly within reports instead of maintaining separate documentation. Notes appear in the definition page, matrix overview, printed reports with synchronized numbering, and Excel exports.

title: Cumulative Updates for Business Central – versions
summary: Cumulative updates for Business Central replace previous releases and fix vulnerabilities across all versions. The post provides links to hotfixes for each version, from v14 (2019 Wave 1) through v28 (2026 Wave 1), noting that administrators should install the latest update.

title: ⚙️ GitHub Copilot: Workspace-Level Control Over AI Context 🔄
summary: GitHub Copilot allows developers to organize and control AI context at the workspace level by enabling or disabling instructions, prompts, agents, and skills per project or client through settings.json configuration. This prevents style guidelines and rules from one client or project from interfering with work on another.

title: 🧠 Agent Skills + MCPs: check your BC extension health in VS Code 🔍
summary: Agent Skills are reusable instruction packages in VS Code that orchestrate external tools like YAMPI and BC Telemetry Buddy to analyze Business Central extension health across environments. A three-level loading model activates only relevant skills without penalizing context, enabling developers to check extension status, versions, deployments, and lifecycle events in production through a single chat message.

title: AL Language extension for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central – versions
summary: AL Language extension changelog documenting features added across versions 15.0 through 18.0, including implicit type conversions, HTTP mocking in tests, multiline strings, JSON accessors, AppSourceCop rules, namespace documentation, and improved IDE capabilities in Visual Studio Code.

title: New Application Ideas of Dynamics 365 Business Central (2026 FEB)
summary: A compilation of feature request ideas submitted by the Business Central community for potential improvements across multiple areas including Copilot and agents, data migration, development, financial management, and various operational modules. The post organizes suggestions by functional area to help prioritize enhancements.

title: ⚡ “Compacting conversation…” small message, big impact on your session 🔄
summary: VSCode automatically compacts agent conversation history when the context window approaches its limit to maintain session continuity. You can manually control compaction with the /compact command or start a fresh session, balancing between preserving context and maintaining response quality.

title: 🔍 Field Magnifier for BC: Enhanced Accessibility 👓
summary: A contextual field magnifier extension for Business Central improves readability by displaying magnified field content in a floating popup on hover, with three adjustable zoom levels (3x, 4x, 5x), without affecting the rest of the interface.

title: 🚫 Never Publish an AL Extension with Missing Translations Again
summary: A VS Code extension that validates translation files are present before publishing AL extensions, manages regional language variants, and visually highlights incomplete translations. It helps developers prevent missing translations for required markets.

title: 🪝 VS Code Agent Hooks: Give Copilot Context Before the First Message
summary: VS Code Agent Hooks allow developers to automatically run scripts at specific lifecycle events to provide dynamic context to AI agents before and during sessions. The post demonstrates how to use SessionStart and PreCompact hooks to ask onboarding questions, store answers, and reinject context when conversations are compacted, enabling agents to adapt their behavior based on project type, technology stack, and experience level.

title: New Application Ideas of Dynamics 365 Business Central (2026 MAR)
summary: A curated collection of community-submitted feature ideas for Dynamics 365 Business Central organized by functional area, covering improvements across finance, sales, purchasing, inventory, manufacturing, development, administration, and localization for the March 2026 release cycle.

title: New Application Ideas of Dynamics 365 Business Central (2026 APR)
summary: This post collects application ideas and feature requests submitted by the community for Dynamics 365 Business Central as of April 2026, covering areas from finance and sales to warehousing and localization.

title: 🔍 Visualize your AL objects in a tree view, filter and navigate directly in VS Code
summary: AL Object Visualizer is a VS Code extension that displays AL objects in a filterable tree view with customizable badges and colors, helping developers navigate and manage multiple files across projects efficiently.

title: 🧠 Global memory for your VS Code agent: preferences that follow you
summary: VS Code agents can use a built-in memory system with three scope levels (user, repository, and session) to store preferences and context that persist across conversations. This feature helps agents remember user preferences, project conventions, and temporary task context automatically in future sessions.

title: New Application Ideas of Dynamics 365 Business Central (2026 MAY)
summary: A curated list of feature ideas and improvement suggestions submitted by the Business Central community for May 2026, covering areas including agents and Copilot, data migrations, financial management, inventory, warehousing, sales, purchasing, and localization enhancements.

title: 🪶 How to slim down the prompt and spend fewer credits in Github Copilot
summary: GitHub Copilot switched to token-based billing on June 1, 2026. The post explains how to reduce credit spending through context optimization (cleaning tools and extensions), developing efficient chat habits (shorter threads, avoiding redundant file pasting), selecting appropriate models and reasoning effort levels, and matching task complexity to the right mode (Ask, Plan, or Agent).

title: World Cup in Business Central: predictions and results ⚽🥅
summary: A World Cup prediction extension for Business Central that lets users share forecasts, track matches imported from a JSON source, register predictions, and compete on a leaderboard with automatic scoring based on exact scores or correct outcomes.

title: 💸The answer is the expensive part: controlling output tokens
summary: Output tokens cost 6× more than input tokens in large language models, making it essential to control what Copilot writes rather than just what you send. The post explains hidden reasoning tokens and provides practical habits and prompt instructions to reduce output costs when using Copilot for AL development and code changes.

title: New Application Ideas of Dynamics 365 Business Central (2026 JUN)
summary: This post lists community-submitted application ideas and feature requests for Dynamics 365 Business Central (June 2026 release), organized by functional areas including Copilot agents, financial management, inventory, sales, and warehouse management.

title: 🧭 Page Explorer for Business Central: everything a page hides, in plain sight
summary: Page Explorer is an AL extension that displays all fields and actions available on a Business Central page in a single window, showing their current values, descriptions, and tooltips. It uses the native Page Summary Provider codeunit to parse page metadata and helps users understand page structure and available options.

title: 🔎 Change Log Blame View: View change history in a different way
summary: The Change Log Blame View extension reorganizes standard change log data into a matrix-style view where rows represent fields and columns represent events, making it easier to track when specific record values changed, by whom, and why.

title: New Application Ideas of Dynamics 365 Business Central (2026 JUL)
summary: A compilation of application improvement ideas for Dynamics 365 Business Central submitted by the community, covering areas like Copilot and agents, financial management, development, inventory, manufacturing, sales, and administration. The post serves as a feature request collection spanning multiple system modules.

title: 🧩 Deriving dimensions in Business Central beyond Default Dimensions
summary: The OnAfterGetRecDefaultDimIDProcedure integration event in the DimensionManagement codeunit fires after Business Central calculates default dimensions, allowing you to extend or modify dimension sets with custom logic. This approach demonstrates five scenarios: deriving dimensions from document fields, other dimensions, related tables, historical data, and overriding with higher-priority rules.

title: 🧹 Cleaning and anonymizing copies in Business Central: environments, companies, and traceability
summary: A reusable solution for automatically anonymizing sensitive data, marking copied companies, and adjusting settings when copying Business Central environments or companies. It provides table and field configuration, manual or event-triggered execution, and comprehensive logging for audit trails.

title: 🚩 Evidence Flags: More trust signal, fewer words
summary: Evidence Flags is a Copilot skill that adds brief labels to claims to distinguish what is backed by evidence, reported by users, or inferred by the model. It helps when explicitly requested via /ef commands to clarify trust levels in responses without cluttering simple questions.

title: New Application Ideas of Dynamics 365 Business Central (2026 AUG)
summary: A collection of feature improvement ideas for Dynamics 365 Business Central submitted by users across multiple areas including agents, development, financial management, inventory, and localization. The post organizes suggestions for enhancements spanning August 2026.

title: BcContainerHelper – versions
summary: BcContainerHelper is a PowerShell module for managing Business Central containers. This post documents release notes for versions 6.1.18 through 5.0.4, covering fixes for PS7 remote session issues, Docker service readiness, test app dependencies, backup operations, NuGet package handling, compiler folder functionality, and numerous other improvements.

title: Visual Studio Code – versions
summary: Visual Studio Code released numerous updates from April 2024 through September 2026, with emphasis on agent-based development, integrated browser tools, AI model flexibility, and enhanced developer productivity features. This helps teams stay current on available coding editor capabilities and AI-assisted development workflows.

title: Integration with Azure Static Web Apps from Business Central
summary: This post explains how to integrate an Azure Static Web App with Business Central by using the WebPageViewer control add-in and the window.postMessage API to enable bidirectional communication between AL code and a hosted web application.

title: Spread the Fire. Don’t Keep It to Yourself.
summary: Knowledge sharing about AI-powered development and tools in Business Central creates value for the entire community rather than diminishing individual advantage. The author argues that transparency about AI workflows, agentic coding techniques, and development tools ultimately builds reputation and opportunities, as demonstrated by successful community projects and client work.

title: Spec-Driven Development — The Way to Build Apps with Agents
summary: Spec-Driven Development is a methodology for building Business Central extensions with AI agents, where structured specifications capture architecture decisions before code is written. This approach maintains consistency across multiple development sessions and prevents agents from reinventing patterns or making conflicting decisions.

title: How to Connect Business Central MCP to Claude Desktop
summary: The post explains how to set up Business Central's native MCP server with Claude Desktop by registering an Entra application, enabling the MCP server in Business Central, and configuring mcp-remote to bridge the connection. This helps AI agents like Claude access Business Central data through a desktop client.

title: Designing Agents for Business Central
summary: The Agent Design Experience in Business Central v27.4 is a sandbox tool for designing, testing, and refining agent instructions, not a low-code deployment platform. Production agents require manual conversion to AL code by exporting the agent XML configuration, creating an AL project with the Agent template, and either following the README instructions or using a coding agent to accelerate the customization process.

title: Install Agent Designer if it is missing
summary: The Agent Designer is included in the 27.4 monthly update and automatically installs in upgraded sandboxes but not production environments. When copying a post-v27.4 production environment to a sandbox, you can manually install the Agent Designer using a specific AppSource URL with its app ID.

title: Business Central Development Serie - Part 1: Introduction
summary: This introduction to a development series explains the importance of architecture, best practices, and long-term maintenance for Business Central extensions, addressing gaps that AI tools alone cannot fill. It covers topics like app types, dependency management, testing, performance, and delivery strategies for developers of all experience levels.

title: Business Central Development Serie - Part 2b: AI for BC Development — The Knowledge Gap That Ships to Production
summary: AI-generated Business Central code can compile and appear functional while containing hidden bugs that silently corrupt data or cause performance issues. Developers must validate AI output across architecture, performance, standard processes, testing, security, and localization before production use, requiring broad domain expertise and proper guardrails.

title: Why API Templates Don't Work on Business Central Custom API Pages
summary: API templates in Business Central only work with specific standard API pages because custom API pages lack the ProcessNewRecordFromAPI function call in their OnInsertRecord trigger. To make templates work on custom API pages, you must add this function call and register fields using the TempFieldSet mechanism.

title: Managing Apps in the Business Central Admin Center
summary: The Manage Apps page in the Business Central admin center controls the stack of apps running on an environment, including the Base Application, Microsoft first-party apps, ISV apps, and per-tenant extensions. You can view, upload, install, update, or uninstall apps depending on their type, though new global apps must be sourced from the marketplace rather than installed directly.

title: Direct transfers from warehouse-enabled locations in Business Central 2026 wave 2
summary: Business Central 2026 wave 2 enables direct transfers to work with warehouse-enabled source locations by supporting outbound warehouse handling and allowing posting method configuration per transfer route instead of company-wide only.

title: Business Central 2026 Wave 2: Preview Images Directly in the Web Client
summary: Business Central 2026 Wave 2 introduces native image preview functionality in the web client, allowing users to view supported image formats (JPEG, PNG, BMP, SVG, WEBP, GIF, AVIF, etc.) directly without downloading. This capability parallels existing PDF preview features and includes support for animated GIFs, clickable thumbnails, and developer access via File.ViewFromStream().

title: Analysis Mode killed half the Excel exports on your client's shared drive
summary: Analysis Mode is a feature that lets users group, filter, and pivot data on Business Central list pages without exporting to Excel. It creates personal analysis views with their own columns, filters, and arrangements that persist between sessions and can be packaged into extensions.

title: How I Recreated the Extension Upload Experience in Business Central
summary: A custom app recreates the deprecated in-product extension upload functionality by calling the Business Central admin center API from AL. It provides a familiar interface for managing extensions with deployment scheduling, schema sync options, and comprehensive logging of all installation operations.

title: Composite Layouts in Business Central 29.0: Brand One Report End to End
summary: Business Central 29.0 enables composite layouts where branding is split into three separate parts (header/footer, theme, and body) that merge at render time instead of baking everything into one Word document. The post walks through a complete example of branding the Standard Sales Invoice report for Contoso, covering setup in both the UI and AL code.

title: BC 29 lets a single index span base table and table extension fields
summary: Business Central 29 allows table extension keys to span both base table and extension fields in a single index, eliminating a long-standing constraint. This enables simpler indexing solutions for filtered lists, reporting extractions, and performance problems that previously required architectural workarounds.

title: How to See When Your SQL Server Backup or Restore Will Finish
summary: A SQL Server query shows the estimated completion time for active backup or restore operations by converting the estimated_completion_time value to a readable clock time. This helps database administrators know when long-running operations will finish instead of guessing.

title: Approval Workflows for Item Journals and Requisition Worksheets
summary: Business Central 28 introduces approval workflows for item journals, requisition worksheets, and planning worksheets, enabling batch-level approvals before posting or conversion to purchase documents. This closes a gap where these critical inventory and procurement operations previously lacked the approval controls available for general journals.

title: Pinned Comment Lines for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central
summary: An extension that displays pinned comments as on-screen notifications when customers, vendors, or items are accessed, ensuring important notes reach users where decisions are made instead of remaining hidden in the comment sheet.

title: Public Preview for Business Central 29.0 (2026 Release Wave 2) Is Here
summary: Business Central 2026 release wave 2 (version 29.0) preview environments are now available for testing. Partners and customers should test their AL extensions, integrations, and customizations against the new version before it becomes production to catch breaking changes and issues early.

title: Dynamics NAV, GP and SL: Why I Think Customers Should Start Planning Now
summary: Migration from Dynamics NAV, GP, or SL to Business Central should be planned early rather than waiting until lifecycle deadlines. The post emphasizes that successful migration requires assessing the current environment, deciding what to migrate, cleaning up unnecessary complexity, and redesigning processes for Business Central's architecture rather than simply converting everything.

title: Create Purchase Quotes for Contacts in Business Central
summary: Creating purchase quotes in Business Central now allows selecting contacts that aren't yet linked to vendors, eliminating the need to set up full vendor records upfront. The vendor record is automatically created only when the quote is released or converted to an order, reducing friction in the purchasing workflow.

title: You can't see your stale documents, and that's why they're stale
summary: A Business Central extension called Unposted Document Aging provides a single list combining sales quotes, orders, and unposted invoices organized into priority bands by age and status. Instead of manual Excel reports, it shows which documents are stale and who owns them, with automated daily email digests per salesperson.

title: Create Purchase Orders from Drop Shipments
summary: Business Central 2026 Release Wave 1 (BC28) streamlines drop shipment workflows by adding a Create Purchase Orders action on sales orders, including drop shipment lines in order planning calculations, and introducing dedicated drop shipment actions in the Planning Worksheet page.

title: NAV to Business Central: What Actually Moves, and What Needs to Change?
summary: Moving from Dynamics NAV to Business Central requires two separate projects: a technical upgrade through mandatory waypoints (version 14 and 25) followed by cloud migration via data replication. The process demands converting C/AL customizations to AL extensions and evaluating whether to do a full migration or reimplementation, with data only moving as far as code does.

title: Define Item Attributes for Item Variants
summary: Business Central 2026 release wave 1 (BC28) introduces item attributes at the variant level, allowing each variant to have distinct attribute values instead of inheriting the same values from the parent item. This solves the problem of keeping variant data accurate without creating separate items for each variation.

title: Recently Used Lookup Values Improve Everyday Productivity (BC29)
summary: Business Central 2026 Release Wave 2 introduces Recently Used in Lookups, which surfaces frequently searched or selected records directly in lookup dialogs to reduce repetitive searches and speed up data entry for common tasks like vendor, customer, and item selection.

title: Business Central Configuration Audit using Vibe Coding
summary: A consultant created a Business Central configuration audit extension using AI-assisted vibe coding to check for 200+ data issues like circular BOMs, missing posting groups, and incomplete setups. The AI agent generated over 5400 lines of code in basic structures, requiring minimal manual adjustments and making the project feasible where writing it manually would have been impractical.

title: Quality Management in Business Central Version 28
summary: Business Central version 28 introduces native quality management functionality that enables inspection of goods across purchase receipts, production, assembly, and sales returns. Organizations can define inspection templates, generate inspections automatically or manually, record results, and enforce quarantine processes - eliminating the need for third-party add-ons for basic quality control requirements.

title: ERP JumpStart: A Better Way to Get Started with Business Central
summary: ERP JumpStart is a guided self-service implementation product for smaller companies transitioning to Business Central. It combines pre-configuration, step-by-step tasks grouped in work packages, and integrated learning content to enable companies to set up and learn the system at their own pace without complex traditional ERP methodology.

title: Approval Workflows in Planning Worksheet
summary: Business Central version 28 adds approval workflow support to planning, requisition, and subcontracting worksheets at the batch level, allowing managers to review and approve suggested actions before they become real purchase orders or production orders. This feature prevents costly mistakes when planners carry out planning suggestions and addresses compliance requirements for segregation of duties.

title: Allow Posting Date Formula
summary: Business Central now supports date formulas for allowed posting dates in General Ledger Setup and User Setup, eliminating the common first-of-month panic when users cannot post transactions outside their allowed date range. This feature allows flexible, formula-based date restrictions that adjust automatically based on the current date.

title: How User and AI Agent Avatars Improve Record Ownership in Business Central BC 28
summary: Business Central BC 28 adds visual avatars for record creators and modifiers on list pages, showing who created or last changed a record without opening the full card. This helps teams identify ownership, reduce duplicate work, and distinguish human-created from AI-generated records.

title: How to Add Currency Symbols to Numeric Fields in Business Central.
summary: BC28 introduces configurable currency symbols on numeric fields to help finance users quickly identify whether transaction amounts are in local or foreign currency. Administrators can choose symbol position and display type globally or per currency without requiring custom development.

title: AI-Part1: what-is-GitHub-copilot-in-vscode-business-central.
summary: GitHub Copilot in VS Code evolved from simple autocomplete to a spectrum of capabilities including inline suggestions, chat, agent mode, and cloud agents. For Business Central AL developers, understanding these distinct modes and their constraints is essential because generic tutorials for other languages don't account for BC-specific patterns like event subscribers, table extensions, and object ID ranges.

title: New ModuleInfo Properties in Business Central 29
summary: Business Central 29 adds four new ModuleInfo properties (Help, EULA, PrivacyStatement, ContextSensitiveHelpUrl) that let AL developers retrieve application manifest metadata programmatically. These properties require runtime 18.0 or later and help extensions avoid duplicating configuration URLs in code.

title: Untangling Your Books: Understanding Application of Entries in Business Central
summary: Application of entries is the process of matching transactions like invoices and payments in Business Central to maintain accurate financial records. The post explains what open entries are, why matching is critical for accounting accuracy, and describes two main application methods: manual application and applying during payment posting.

title: How to Use the Copy Location Feature in Business Central 2026 Wave 1 (BC28)
summary: The Copy Location feature in Business Central BC28 allows users to duplicate existing warehouse and location configurations instead of setting them up manually, reducing implementation time and standardizing setups across multiple locations.

title: How Business Central 2026 Improves Item Variant Management with Pictures and Attributes.
summary: Business Central 2026 adds pictures and variant-level attributes to item variants, enabling faster product identification and more accurate product information management. This helps organizations with multiple product variations reduce errors and maintain better inventory data.

title: How to Email Posted Sales Shipments and Return Receipts in Business Central 2026 Wave 1.
summary: Business Central 2026 Wave 1 adds email delivery, PDF generation, and attachment management for Posted Sales Shipments and Posted Return Receipts, enabling organizations to send shipment confirmations and return documentation directly from the system instead of relying on manual exports and external email.

title: Manage Database Index Usage in Business Central.
summary: Business Central 2026 Wave 1 enables administrators to manage database indexes directly from the client without SQL access. The feature allows viewing index metrics, disabling unused secondary indexes per company, and optimizing database storage and write performance.

title: How to Export CSV Files from Business Central Using CSV Buffer (Developer Guide)
summary: This guide explains how to export data from Business Central to CSV format using the CSV Buffer table, covering its structure, recommended architecture, common export issues, and performance best practices for developers building integration and data exchange solutions.

title: Business Central 2026 Release Wave 2 Preview Is Now Available
summary: Business Central 2026 release wave 2 (version 29.0) preview is now available for testing by customers, partners, developers, and consultants to validate solutions and report issues before production rollout.

title: AI-Part2: Setup-Vscode-al-copilot-business-central
summary: Setting up Visual Studio Code, the AL Language extension, and GitHub Copilot for Business Central AL development requires installation of three components and verification of connections. This post guides developers through each setup step and highlights common gotchas like extension version mismatches and separate subscription management.

title: How to Use Date Formulas for Allowed Posting Periods in Business Central BC28.
summary: Business Central BC28 introduces dynamic date formulas for allowed posting periods that automatically calculate posting windows based on the current date instead of requiring manual updates. Administrators can configure these formulas in General Ledger Setup, User Setup, and Journal Templates to automate posting restrictions and reduce monthly maintenance.

title: Business Central 2026 Release Wave 1 Installation Guide: Requirements, Prerequisites, and Setup Walkthrough
summary: Business Central 2026 Release Wave 1 (BC28) installation requires Windows 11 or Windows Server 2022/2025, .NET 8, SQL Server compatibility level 160/170, and 16 GB RAM minimum. This guide details system prerequisites, hardware requirements, software components, and a step-by-step installation process to help consultants and administrators avoid common deployment issues.

title: Business Central 29.0: Major Change to Table Extensions and SQL Storage.
summary: Business Central 29.0 changes how table extension fields are stored in the database, moving from a companion-table model to storing extension fields directly in the same SQL table as the base table. This enables cross-table indexes, can improve query performance, and requires developers to avoid direct SQL dependencies.

title: Automating Posting Periods in Business Central with Date Formulas
summary: Date formulas enable automatic posting period adjustments in Business Central based on today's date instead of fixed dates. This feature applies to General Ledger Setup, User Setup, and General Journal Templates, reducing manual updates and posting errors.

title: Preview Images Directly in the Business Central Web Client
summary: Business Central now supports previewing image attachments directly in the web client without downloading. The feature works with multiple image formats across attachments, agents, email, and FactBox thumbnails, with developers using File.ViewFromStream (online) or File.View (on-premises) to integrate the functionality into extensions.

title: How to Group and Consolidate General Journal Lines Using Query Object in Business Central.
summary: This post explains how to consolidate General Journal Lines in Business Central using Query Objects to group records by Posting Date, Account No., and Dimension Set ID, then aggregate amounts and insert consolidated results into a target journal batch. It addresses a common developer scenario where multiple journal lines with identical keys need to be combined.

title: Directions Asia 2026 Recap: Key Takeaways from Ho Chi Minh City
summary: Directions Asia 2026 in Ho Chi Minh City focused on AI's transformation of Business Central from a system of record to a system of action, with live demonstrations of autonomous agents for accounts payable, sales orders, and expenses. The conference highlighted emerging partner competencies in agent design, integration architecture evolution, and governance frameworks needed for AI-driven implementations.

title: Evolve AL Interfaces with Default Implementations in Business Central 29.0
summary: Business Central 29.0 introduces default method implementations for AL interfaces, allowing interface contracts to evolve without immediately breaking existing implementations. The feature works with RequiredPending and analyzer rules to create a staged migration path where interface authors can add new methods with fallback behavior and gradually require explicit implementations over time.

title: Business Central ToolTip and ToolTipML Properties Are Now Available on Pages
summary: Business Central now supports ToolTip and ToolTipML properties directly on page objects, allowing navigation actions to inherit tooltips from their target pages rather than requiring duplicate tooltip definitions on each action.

title: Business Central Version 29: Recently Searched in Tell Me and Recently Used Lookups
summary: Business Central Version 29 introduces Recently Searched in Tell Me and Recently Used Lookups to help users navigate faster and enter data more efficiently. These personalized features reduce repetitive searching and clicks by surfacing frequently accessed pages and records based on user behavior patterns.

title: AL Language Tests: An Executable Spec for How BC Actually Behaves
summary: The BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests repository creates an executable specification of AL language behavior by running tests against real BC service tiers across multiple versions. It ensures AL Runner (an AL emulator) behaves accurately and provides a reference for undocumented AL features verified by CI.

title: AL Runner: A Weekend of Autonomous Agents, a Windows Cross-Check, and 59% of Microsoft's Tests Passing
summary: AL Runner, a testing framework for Business Central, achieved significant progress through autonomous agent loops over a weekend, adding 832 new tests and implementing a Windows cross-check workflow that discovered platform-level differences between Linux and Windows BC instances. The suite now passes 59% of Microsoft's 40,530 base-app tests, revealing both permission configuration issues and genuine behavioral differences that need addressing.

title: AL Runner v2.2 and v2.3: Coverage, Quick Scripts, and a Watch Mode You Can Trust
summary: AL Runner v2.2 and v2.3 added code coverage reporting, a quick-script execute command for testing snippets without a codeunit, and fixed a watch mode that was recompiling mid-save during file bursts. The releases also included roughly 130 behavioral fixes to align the runner with real Business Central, with startup performance improvements.

title: AL Runner: Run AL Unit Tests Without a BC Service Tier
summary: AL Runner is a CLI tool that transpiles AL code to C# and executes unit tests in-memory without a BC service tier, Docker, or SQL Server, completing test runs in seconds instead of 20-30 minutes. It uses the BC compiler's public API to convert AL objects to C#, rewrites runtime types with mocks, and compiles everything with Roslyn for fast local testing.

title: AL Runner: Testing Against Real Cronus Data, Debugging Restored, and Mutation-Ready Coverage
summary: AL Runner, a testing tool for Business Central AL code, now supports testing against real Cronus demo data via the --test-data flag, restores breakpoint debugging through Debug Adapter Protocol, enables per-test coverage attribution for mutation testing, and introduces TDD mode for agentic development workflows.

title: AL Runner v2: What Feedback Told Me v1 Was Missing
summary: AL Runner v2 introduces a fundamental architecture change that enables integration testing against real Microsoft and third-party dependencies instead of mocks, moving from type-renaming and stubbing to using BC's own compiler and patching only low-level database operations. The update emphasizes fail-loudly error handling so tests cannot silently pass with wrong results, and introduces a separate language behavior test suite that validates all tests against real Business Central before trusting them.

title: If You Can't Make It Fast, Make It Feel Fast
summary: When operations take time despite optimization, BC developers can make them feel faster by moving blocking work to the background instead of waiting for user input. The post explores four background processing tools (Page Background Tasks, StartSession, TaskScheduler, and Job Queue), their use cases, and how BC online's auto-scaling distributes batch workloads across server instances to keep UI sessions responsive.

title: Introducing bc-code-atlas: Real BC Source for Coding Agents, Not a Guess
summary: bc-code-atlas is an MCP server that provides AI coding agents with grounded, verifiable access to BC's Base Application source code across versions and countries, eliminating hallucinations by linking every result back to real AL files through semantic search and exact-source lookups.

title: BC on Linux: A Working Web Client, Faster Boots, Local Dev on Mac and Linux, and a Fast Lane in AL-Go
summary: Running Business Central on Linux now supports a working web client for local development, achieving cold boot times of 79 seconds and test runs of 1,067 tests in 69 seconds. The project includes AL-Go integration with a Linux fast lane for pull requests and snapshot-based caching for even faster development cycles.

title: Introducing bcdb: Read a Business Central Backup Without SQL Server
summary: bcdb is a tool that reads SQL Server backup files (.bak) and Business Central cloud exports (.bacpac) directly without requiring SQL Server or a restore process. It decodes table data using AL field names when provided with extension symbols and supports library and CLI usage.

title: bcdb restore: Write a Cloud Export Into a Container
summary: The bcdb restore tool writes cloud exports directly into a running Docker container without requiring matching schemas, intelligently handling mismatches by skipping missing tables and columns. It restored a production environment in 10 seconds and supports flexible identity table handling, company mapping, and dry-run preview modes.

title: Building a Plug & Play Claude Code Dev Container for AL Development
summary: Setting up a reusable dev container that runs Claude Code with AL development tools installed, persistent authentication across rebuilds, and network isolation to safely use Claude Code with dangerous permissions enabled in a sandboxed environment.

title: Claude Code in a Standalone Docker Container: Building a Real Sandbox (Part 2)
summary: This post describes building a secure standalone Docker container for Claude Code that eliminates VS Code IPC attack surfaces by using docker run directly instead of dev containers. The setup includes firewall rules, credential stripping, volume mounting for project directories, and per-language instruction file injection to isolate Claude Code while allowing local commits but blocking network access to external hosts.

title: Introducing ALCops — LinterCop's Next Chapter
summary: ALCops is a complete replacement for LinterCop that splits code analysis into six domain-specific analyzers (ApplicationCop, DocumentationCop, FormattingCop, LinterCop, PlatformCop, TestAutomationCop) to address structural limitations including GitHub rate limits, overgrown feature scope, and rule severity constraints. It improves code quality through better rule severity defaults, 30 code fixes, correctness fixes, and distributes via NuGet with MCP server support for AI tooling integration.

title: I Can Turn Off My Code. I Can't Turn Off Yours.
summary: When developers set RunTrigger to false on Insert, Modify, or DeleteAll, they silently disable all subscribers including base app code and third-party extensions. The post argues that triggers should run by default because developers cannot know at compile time what logic they would disable, and proposes the platform should dynamically check at runtime whether anything is registered on a trigger before deciding whether to skip the expensive per-row execution.

title: Optimizing BC Code History Downloads with HTTP Range Requests
summary: Optimizing the MSDyn365BC.Sandbox.Code.History repository's daily download pipeline by fixing silent failures in PowerShell scripts and implementing HTTP Range requests to reduce bandwidth usage from 800MB-2GB+ per country artifact to roughly 120MB, cutting cumulative compute time by 86% across 50 parallel countries.

title: Swappable Claude Profiles: Per-Project Configs via Container Mounting (Part 3)
summary: Claude Code profiles enable project-specific configurations by mounting host directories as ~/.claude inside containers, allowing separate contexts, instructions, and agents for different work types. The profile system makes it practical to maintain AL development, telemetry investigation, and other specialized contexts without switching tools.

title: Turning My Coding Streams Into Blog Posts (With a Little Help From Claude)
summary: A developer built a Claude Code skill to automatically convert YouTube live streams into blog posts by downloading captions and frames, then having Claude write structured articles. The pipeline also enriches posts with documentation links, improving discoverability for both readers and AI tools like CentralQ.

title: You don't need the base app to run your unit tests
summary: Unit tests for self-contained Business Central logic do not require the base application to run. By structuring code as isolated sub-extensions with their own app.json files and only platform dependencies, developers can significantly reduce container startup time and pipeline costs.

title: Weekly Recap: August 7-14
summary: A weekly recap covering AL Runner v2 improvements closing emulation gaps against real BC, reference suite growth through sandbox-verified testing, bc-code-atlas enhancements for cross-app call graphs with deterministic global IDs, AL-Go fast lane hardening for multi-workflow stability, and compile-time benchmarking showing NuGet-sourced compilation is faster due to smaller dependency caches.

title: Weekly Recap: August 14-21
summary: This weekly recap covers AL Runner releases (v2.2-v2.3.1) with coverage reporting and watch mode improvements, CI/CD fixes for parallel dependency resolution and Linux builds, a major catch-up of bc-code-atlas's stale graphify-al fork that revealed hidden AL-specific behaviors and tree-sitter parser changes, and various smaller tool fixes. It highlights infrastructure improvements that prevent silent failures in builds and dependency resolution.

title: Weekly Recap: August 21-28
summary: Weekly recap covering AL Runner CI tooling fixes, Linux fast lane pipeline bugs, a major OpenPageInspection browser extension rewrite for cross-browser support, and Azure CLI authentication contributions to the navapi Business Central API client.

title: BC Friday Tips #65 Freeze Column Property
summary: The FreezeColumn property keeps selected columns visible when users scroll horizontally through list pages with many fields, reducing the need for horizontal scrolling and keeping important data in view.

title: BC Friday Tips #66 API v2 app
summary: The Exclude_APIV2 app is a hidden Microsoft extension in Business Central that contains standard API V2 objects. Developers can explore this app via symbol files in VS Code to understand Microsoft's API design patterns and reference it when building or extending their own APIs.

title: BC Friday Tips #67 Reset Page Number in RDLC
summary: The ResetPageNumber property in RDLC reports restarts page numbering at 1 for each group or document, matching user expectations when printing multiple groups.

title: BC Friday Tips #68 Always Use Field Validation
summary: Field validation in Business Central extensions ensures all business logic runs and prevents data corruption when other apps subscribe to validation events. Bypassing validation can create hidden bugs by skipping trigger logic even when fields appear correct.

title: BC Friday Tips #69 Item Blocked Fields
summary: The Item table in Business Central has multiple blocked fields (Blocked, Sales Blocked, Purchasing Blocked, Service Blocked) that control item restrictions. Checking only the main Blocked field can miss module-specific restrictions and cause logic errors.

title: BC Friday Tips #70 Email Scenario Attachment
summary: Email scenarios in Business Central can include default attachments that are automatically sent with every email, such as terms and conditions attached to invoice emails. This prevents missed attachments and ensures consistent communication without requiring manual user action each time.

title: BC Friday Tips #71 BlankZero Property
summary: The BlankZero property on numeric fields can be set to true to display empty values instead of zero, reducing visual clutter and helping users focus on meaningful data in optional fields.

title: BC Friday Tips #72 Inlay Hints
summary: Inlay Hints in VS Code display inline parameter names and return types while coding in AL, helping developers understand function signatures without hovering or jumping to definitions. This feature is particularly useful for procedures with many parameters and can be configured to appear on demand to keep the editor clean.

title: BC Friday Tips #73 Show All Configuration Package Errors
summary: When applying a Configuration Package in Business Central, users can view all errors on a single page by clicking the Error section, allowing faster review and resolution without checking entries individually.

title: BC Friday Tips #74 Copy Document and Custom Field
summary: When adding custom fields to Sales Header or Sales Invoice Header tables, developers must consider how the Copy Document feature will handle those fields. The post explains that custom fields are automatically copied along with documents, requiring developers to decide whether values should be copied, cleared, or recalculated to maintain data integrity.

title: BC Friday Tips #75 Dynamics BC Excel Reports
summary: Excel Reports objects in Business Central belong to the Dynamics BC Excel Reports extension rather than the Base Application, requiring developers to add it as a dependency when extending these objects.

title: BC Friday Tips #76 Barcode Fonts in RDL Reports
summary: Creating barcodes in Business Central SaaS reports requires setting the FontFamily property directly in RDL files without installing fonts locally. This approach works out of the box and supports various barcode types like Code 93 using fonts such as IDAutomationC93M.

title: BC Friday Tips #77 TestField Show Record Action
summary: TestField automatically adds a Show Record button to error dialogs when field validation fails, letting users jump directly to the problem record. This feature works natively for tables with single primary keys like Customer, but not for compound primary key tables like Sales Header.

title: BC Friday Tips #78 InitValue Property
